title: The Great Prophecy
text:
A half-blood of the eldest gods
Shall reach sixteen against all odds
And see the world in cursed sleep
A hero's soul, cursed blade shall reap
A single choice shall end his days
Olympus to preserve or raze.
interpretation_notes: Delivered originally to May Castellan during her failed attempt to receive the Oracle's spirit. Believed by Chiron and Camp Half-Blood for years to refer strictly to Percy Jackson destroying or saving Olympus. In reality, while Percy reached sixteen and made the single choice to hand Annabeth's cursed dagger to Luke Castellan, it was Luke whose soul was reaped when he sacrificed himself to destroy Kronos.
description: The foundational prophecy governing the entire five-book arc of Percy Jackson and the Olympians.

title: The Lightning Thief Prophecy
text:
You shall go west, and face the god who has turned,
You shall find what was stolen, and see it safely returned,
You shall be betrayed by one who calls you a friend,
And you shall fail to save what matters most, in the end.
interpretation_notes: Delivered to Percy Jackson in the Attic of the Big House. Percy traveled west to Los Angeles and faced Ares (the turned god). He retrieved Zeus's Master Bolt and Hades's Helm of Darkness. Luke Castellan was the friend who betrayed him. Percy failed to rescue his mother from the Underworld using the pearls, though she saved herself using Medusa's severed head on Gabe Ugliano.
description: The prophecy issued for Percy Jackson's first quest to recover the stolen Master Bolt.

title: The Sea of Monsters Prophecy
text:
You shall sail the iron ship with warriors of bone,
You shall find what you seek and make it your own,
But despair for your life entombed within stone,
And fail without friends, to fly home alone.
interpretation_notes: Delivered to Clarisse La Rue for the Quest for the Golden Fleece. Clarisse commanded the CSS Birmingham (manned by zombie soldiers), retrieved the Fleece from Polyphemus's cave (entombed in stone), and relied on Percy, Annabeth, Tyson, and Grover to escape. Percy sent Clarisse back alone on an airplane with the Fleece to ensure the final line's literal fulfillment.
description: Prophecy guiding the quest into the Sea of Monsters to recover the Golden Fleece and heal Thalia's pine tree.

title: The Titan's Curse Prophecy
text:
Five shall go west to the goddess in chains,
One shall be lost in the land without rain,
The bane of Olympus shows the trail,
Campers and Hunters combined prevail,
The Titan's curse must one withstand,
And one shall perish by a parent's hand.
interpretation_notes: Delivered when the mummy of the Oracle walked out of the Big House into the woods. Five companions went west. Bianca di Angelo died in the Junkyard of Hephaestus (land without rain). The Ophiotaurus (bane of Olympus) guided them. Campers and Hunters fought together. Percy held the weight of the sky (the Titan's curse) before Artemis forced Atlas back under it. Zoë Nightshade died from a fatal blow struck by her father Atlas.
description: Prophecy issued to Zoë Nightshade for the quest to rescue the goddess Artemis and Annabeth Chase.

title: The Labyrinth Prophecy
text:
You shall delve in the darkness of the endless maze,
The dead, the traitor, and the lost one raise.
You shall rise or fall by the ghost king's hand,
The child of Athena's final stand.
Destroy with a hero's final breath,
And lose a love to worse than death.
interpretation_notes: Delivered to Annabeth Chase. The quest team raised spirits of the dead (via Nico), encountered the traitor Ethan Nakamura, and found the fading god Pan (the lost one). Nico (the ghost king) chose to help the demigods. Daedalus (child of Athena) sacrificed his life (hero's final breath) to destroy the Labyrinth tied to his soul. Annabeth lost Luke to Kronos's demonic possession (worse than death).
description: Prophecy given to Annabeth Chase for the quest to navigate Daedalus's subterranean Labyrinth.

title: The Prophecy of the Seven
text:
Seven half-bloods shall answer the call,
To storm or fire, the world must fall.
An oath to keep with a final breath,
And foes bear arms to the Doors of Death.
interpretation_notes: Spoken by Rachel Elizabeth Dare in a green-mist trance immediately after she accepted the Spirit of Delphi at Camp Half-Blood. Serves as the Second Great Prophecy setting up the Heroes of Olympus series.
description: The Second Great Prophecy delivered at the conclusion of the Titan War.

title: The Prophecy of the Sword of Hades
text:
Child of May, beware the shade,
Stolen power, the forged blade.
Three shall venture to the deep,
One shall wake what ought to sleep.
interpretation_notes: Delivered to Percy Jackson, Thalia Grace, and Nico di Angelo in The Demigod Files. 'Child of May' refers to Percy (born in August, but summoned in May) or Hermes's son Luke. 'Stolen power' refers to Hades's secret sword equipped with a Key of Death stolen by Ethan Nakamura. 'One shall wake what ought to sleep' refers to Iapetus (Bob) being summoned before being dipped in the River Lethe.
description: Prophecy guiding the Underworld mission to recover Hades's secret weapon.

title: Prophecy of the Bones of Mother Earth
text: When you leave this place, cover your heads and throw the bones of your mother behind you as you go, and do not look back.
interpretation_notes: Recounted in Percy Jackson's Greek Gods. Deucalion and Pyrrha realized that 'mother' referred to Mother Earth (Gaea) and 'bones' referred to stones. Throwing stones over their shoulders repopulated humanity after the Great Flood.
description: Ancient mythic prophecy given to Deucalion and Pyrrha following the Great Flood.

title: Prophecy of King Acrisius
text: You will never have sons. One day your daughter Danaë will have a son. That boy will kill you and become the next king of Argos.
interpretation_notes: Recounted in Percy Jackson's Greek Heroes. King Acrisius imprisoned Danaë in a bronze tower, but Zeus visited her in a shower of gold, conceiving Perseus. Years later, Perseus accidentally killed Acrisius with an errant discus throw during an athletic contest.
description: Mythic prophecy foretelling King Acrisius's death by his grandson Perseus.

title: Prophecy of Psyche's Doom
text: Your daughter shall marry no mortal. She is destined to marry a monster—a fierce, barbaric beast even the gods fear! Dress her for her wedding as you would dress her for her funeral. Take her to the tallest spire of rock in your kingdom. There she shall meet her doom!
interpretation_notes: Recounted in Percy Jackson's Greek Heroes. Aphrodite sought to punish Psyche for her beauty, but Eros fell in love with Psyche and used the Oracle to have her placed on a mountain peak where Zephyrus carried her to Eros's hidden palace.
description: Mythic prophecy regarding Psyche's divine marriage to Eros.

title: Prophecy of Eurystheus and Hercules
text: Go to the city of Tiryns. Serve High King Eurystheus by doing ten great tasks of his choosing.
interpretation_notes: Recounted in Percy Jackson's Greek Heroes. Delivered to Hercules after Hera drove him to temporary madness. Fulfilling the tasks resulted in the legendary Twelve Labors of Hercules.
description: Mythic prophecy binding Hercules to King Eurystheus for his Labors.
